events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) misses Wednesday practice; Minter won't rule him out for Atlanta, Zay Flowers limited
events.detail: Jackson did not practice Wednesday with the ankle sprain from Week 4. Jesse Minter said his status for Sunday at Atlanta will be evaluated through the week and would not rule him out even if he misses every practice. Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited per the Baltimore Sun; Rashod Bateman also sat. Ian Rapoport had earlier called Week 5 an "outside chance."
events.so_what: Still a forecast, not a ruling: hold Jackson and plan a Week 5 fallback QB, since the konami rushing floor is what makes him a weekly start and a sprained ankle is exactly what removes it even if he suits up. Tyler Huntley would start if he sits. Flowers practicing at all is the better sign of the two, but a Huntley start lowers his ceiling.

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase still in concussion protocol Wednesday; Tee Higgins (adductor) limited, with a Week 6 bye behind it
events.detail: Chase remained in the protocol Wednesday and must clear all five phases, including a full practice, to play at Miami. Higgins was a limited participant. With Andrei Iosivas on IR and Colbie Young hurt, Dohnte Meyers (7-82 on nine targets in Week 4) is the top healthy wideout if both sit. The Bengals are on bye in Week 6.
events.so_what: Higgins practicing at all moves him from likely out to a real Friday decision; Chase still reads as a Week 5 fallback plan. Either way the Week 6 bye means both are gone for two straight weekends for anyone counting on them in the FLEX, so bench depth with a Week 5 and Week 6 game matters more than usual.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Buccaneers rule out Baker Mayfield (thumb) for Thursday at Dallas; Jalon Daniels makes his second start
events.detail: Tampa Bay officially ruled out Mayfield for Thursday night, along with S Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), CB Benjamin Morrison (quad) and LB SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot). Rookie Jalon Daniels starts again after a 148-yard, one-TD, two-INT debut against Green Bay.
events.so_what: Mayfield is a confirmed zero this week and needs replacing before Thursday kickoff, not Sunday. A rookie at QB caps every Bucs pass catcher; start them on role, not ceiling. The Dallas defense facing Daniels without three Tampa defensive starters on the other side is a fine DEF streaming spot.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Tank Dell returns to Texans practice, opening his 21-day activation window
events.detail: Dell practiced Wednesday for the first time this regular season after opening the year on IR, recovering from the multi-ligament knee injury he suffered in December 2024. Houston now has 21 days to activate him or leave him on IR. No game date has been set.
events.so_what: Not a lineup option yet; he is a stash. A bench stash costs one of only five bench spots, so it is worth it only on a roster that can carry a no-points slot for two or three weeks.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) DNP Wednesday; Chris Olave sits on a listed rest day; Tyler Shough (left hand) also out
events.detail: The Saints' Wednesday report (a walk-through, so estimated) lists Kamara DNP with a back injury; Kellen Moore said the knee Kamara hurt Monday night checked out fine and the issue is back soreness. Olave, hurt on the final drive of an 8-116 night, is listed "NIR-Rest," not injured. QB Tyler Shough is DNP with a left-hand injury and TE Noah Fant is limited (abdomen). Travis Etienne remains on IR.
events.so_what: Olave's tag is the good news: a rest day is not an injury designation. Kamara is a Friday call on a new body part at his age; anyone starting him should line up a Sunday fallback. Shough's non-throwing hand is the quiet one to watch, since a QB change would cap every Saints pass catcher.

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) and D'Andre Swift (hip, knee) both miss Bears practice Wednesday
events.detail: Both Bears backs sat out Wednesday. Ben Johnson had called Monangai "day-to-day" after his 30-carry, two-TD game against the Jets, and reporting so far suggests no real concern about his Week 5 status against Green Bay. Tyson Bagent starts at QB with Caleb Williams out.
events.so_what: Monangai is the volume back here and is still on track; no move yet. If Thursday shows another DNP for him, the backfield gets murky fast with Swift also limited, and a Bagent-led offense lowers the scoring ceiling for both.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Jayden Daniels (elbow) practices in full Wednesday, on track to start vs. Giants; Mariota (MCL) avoids IR
events.detail: Daniels was a full participant Wednesday and Washington is aiming to start him Sunday against the Giants; he will wear a brace on his left arm. Marcus Mariota sprained his right MCL in London and will not go on IR, but did not practice. Dan Quinn had said Daniels needed a full practice week to play.
events.so_what: Still a forecast until Friday's report clears him, but a full Wednesday is the strongest signal yet. If he plays, his rushing is the konami premium that makes him a QB1; note his top two receivers both sat Wednesday (separate item), which caps the passing ceiling this week.

source.label: Yahoo Sports Week 5 injury report, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) limited Wednesday ahead of New Orleans; Jordan Addison sits with soreness
events.detail: Jefferson, who missed Week 4 against Miami with an ankle sprain, was a limited participant Wednesday. Addison did not practice; Kevin O'Connell called his soreness minor. Odell Beckham Jr. signed to Minnesota's practice squad the same day.
events.so_what: Limited on Wednesday is the first real step toward a Week 5 return, but it is still a Friday call. Do not drop Addison over a minor-soreness DNP; plan around Jefferson only once he carries no designation.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) misses Giants practice Wednesday, calls himself "sore"
events.detail: Nabers did not practice Wednesday with a knee injury, per Giants.com's Dan Salomone. He said he did "as much as I could," called the soreness different from what he usually feels, and answered "we'll see" on Sunday at Washington. He also said his shoulder is a little sore, though the team listed only the knee. He is a year removed from tearing his right ACL and is coming off a 112-yard game against Arizona.
events.so_what: Treat as a genuine risk until he practices: a WR1 coming off a major knee injury does not get the benefit of the doubt. Line up a FLEX fallback with a Sunday game now rather than scrambling Friday.

source.label: CBS Sports (via Giants.com's Dan Salomone), Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Chase McLaughlin cleared to kick Thursday at Dallas, no game designation after a full practice
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 6 item. McLaughlin (right groin/hip) missed Tuesday's walkthrough but was a full participant Wednesday and carries no designation on the final report. Todd Bowles told reporters he will play Thursday. He was 9 of 9 on field goals with a long of 59 entering the week. Baker Mayfield, Antoine Winfield Jr., Benjamin Morrison and SirVocea Dennis are out for Tampa Bay.
events.so_what: Start him as normal; the fallback-kicker scramble is off. His value rests on long makes scoring the top distance bands, and a groin on the plant leg is the one thing worth a glance at warmups, but no designation means the team expects full range.

events.headline: D.J. Moore (shoulder) sits out Wednesday practice after his second shoulder exit of the season
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 5 item. Moore did not take part in team practice Wednesday. Adam Schefter had reported the re-aggravated shoulder is not a long-term problem. He first hurt the same shoulder in Week 2. Keon Coleman played 78% of snaps after Moore left the last game.
events.so_what: A Wednesday DNP keeps a missed game in play: have a healthy FLEX ready and wait on Friday's designation. Do not drop him; this reads as a short absence.

source.label: Yahoo Sports Week 5 injury report, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs (hamstrings) both miss Commanders practice Wednesday
events.detail: McLaurin, who hurt his hamstring in practice on Oct. 2 and was inactive for the loss to the Colts in London, did not practice Wednesday. Diggs also did not practice with a hamstring injury. Jayden Daniels (left elbow) practiced in full the same day. Washington hosts the Giants on Sunday.
events.so_what: Two Wednesday DNPs on the same team: neither is a lineup you can set yet, so line up a FLEX fallback before Friday's designations. If both sit, whoever plays outside for Washington inherits the targets of a QB who may be returning with a braced arm, which is a volume bump without much ceiling.

events.headline: Kyren Williams plays 70 snaps to Blake Corum's 13 with a career-high 13 targets in Rams win
events.detail: In the 24-20 comeback over the Eagles, Williams ran 16 times for 80 yards and two TDs and caught 10 of 13 targets for 67 yards. Corum played about 15% of snaps.
events.so_what: This is a workhorse role: every-down snaps, goal-line work and a passing-game share on top. Start him every week as an RB1. Corum is not a meaningful handcuff unless Williams gets hurt.

events.headline: Keon Coleman plays 78% of snaps and goes 6-116-1 after D.J. Moore's shoulder injury; Dalton Kincaid fades
events.detail: With Moore out of the Week 4 game, Coleman played 46 of 59 snaps (up from 48%) and ran 28 routes. Kincaid fell to 35 snaps and 20 routes for two targets as Buffalo leaned on three-wide sets.
events.so_what: Coleman is a starter-grade WR3/FLEX for as long as Moore sits, and a 34-yard TD shows the downfield role. Kincaid's route drop is the bigger warning: at a shallow TE position, 20 routes is not a startable floor.

events.headline: RJ Harvey catches all 10 targets for 68 yards as the Broncos lean on him through the air
events.detail: Harvey ran seven times for 25 yards against San Francisco but caught 10 of 10 targets for 68 yards. His 21.9% target share trails only Bijan Robinson among NFL running backs.
events.so_what: The rushing line is thin, so his value rests on the passing role, and that role looks real. He is a FLEX-grade back on volume in any of these formats; the yardage per touch is low, so do not expect it to hold an RB1 slot.

league_notes.clash: Full PPR here, so 10 catches is worth five more points than in the half-PPR leagues; a receiving share this size makes him a weekly start in this league.

events.headline: Ladd McConkey aggravates his foot at Seattle, called "week-to-week" by Jim Harbaugh
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. McConkey was active against the Seahawks but aggravated the same foot injury that had him questionable, played 24 snaps, failed to catch either of his two targets and was ruled out in the third quarter. Harbaugh called him "week-to-week" on Monday, while ESPN's Kris Rhim reported he may be closer to day-to-day. The first Chargers injury report comes Wednesday. Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris are Justin Herbert's top two wideouts if McConkey sits.
events.so_what: Not a fact you can set a lineup on yet: if he is healthy enough to practice Wednesday he is a FLEX, otherwise plan around him. Johnston is the main beneficiary of any absence; Harris is a speculative add only. The Chargers line is also falling apart (Joe Alt and Trevor Penning both hurt), which caps every Chargers pass catcher.

events.headline: Bijan Robinson (145 yards, 2 TDs) and Brian Robinson (3 TDs) combine for five scores as Falcons rout Saints 45-24
events.detail: On Monday Night Football Bijan Robinson ran 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns, including a 59-yard run. Brian Robinson ran 14 times for 62 yards and scored all three of his touchdowns from inside the 12 (4, 8 and 11 yards). Michael Penix Jr. went 15 of 20 for 233 yards and a touchdown in a game Atlanta controlled throughout. Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews left 11 snaps in.
events.so_what: Bijan stays a locked RB1; the new information is that Brian Robinson owns the short-yardage carries in a blowout script, which makes him a TD-dependent FLEX option in weeks Atlanta is favored rather than a pure handcuff. Do not chase three scores on 62 yards as a stable floor. Watch Matthews' status for the run game.

events.headline: Tyreek Hill expected to sign "over the next few days," agent says; Chiefs among teams in talks
events.detail: Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday he anticipates Hill signing with a team within days. Kansas City reached out Sunday night after losing Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle, 12 to 16 weeks) and Rashee Rice (hamstring, possibly several weeks). Hill is recovering from the dislocated knee and torn ACL he suffered in Week 4 of 2025, and the Chiefs believe he is targeting a November return.
events.so_what: Nothing to start before November. If he lands in Kansas City he walks into a depleted receiver room with Mahomes, which makes him a bench stash worth a spot for anyone with room; anywhere else, wait for a practice before spending one. Rice holders should note a Hill signing would cap Rice's target share once both are healthy.

events.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) could miss several weeks; Tyquan Thornton out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle dislocation
events.detail: Rice pulled up on a first-quarter catch-and-run against the Raiders and did not return. Andy Reid called it a tweak, but The Athletic's Mike Silver reported Rice could be out several weeks. Kansas City has its bye in Week 5, so the first game he can miss is Week 6 against the Chargers. Thornton dislocated his ankle in the fourth quarter and needs surgery, with a possible late-season return.
events.so_what: Hold Rice through the bye and read the Week 6 practice reports; this is a bench stash, not a drop. With Thornton gone for months, the Chiefs' remaining receivers and tight ends absorb Mahomes' targets, so watch which one runs the most routes in Week 6.

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) unlikely before Week 7, with Week 9 the likelier debut
events.detail: Adam Schefter reported the Saints rookie, on IR since a training-camp hamstring injury and eligible to return Tuesday, is weeks away. Week 7 is the best case and Week 9 against Cleveland on Nov. 8 is the likelier target.
events.so_what: A stash only for a team with an open IR slot. He gives no help before November and then has to earn targets in an offense he has not played in yet.

events.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) reported week-to-week and likely out for London vs. Jaguars; Tank Bigsby to IR, Will Shipley next up
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. Monday reporting moved Barkley to week-to-week with the hamstring, and he is considered likely to miss the Week 5 game against the Jaguars in London; Ian Rapoport said it does not initially seem "overly serious" and Nick Sirianni deferred a formal update to Wednesday's first practice. Bigsby, who replaced Barkley on Sunday, will have core-muscle surgery and go on injured reserve, missing at least four games. Will Shipley, who ran six times for 23 yards Sunday, is the only healthy back on the depth chart.
events.so_what: Plan on no Barkley in Week 5 and set the lineup around it rather than waiting on Wednesday. Bigsby is a drop or an IR stash, not the pickup; Shipley is the Eagles back to claim, but Philadelphia will likely add a veteran, so treat him as a one- or two-week volume play. Hold Barkley.

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) won't play Week 5 vs. 49ers; Emanuel Wilson keeps the lead role
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. Mike Macdonald said Monday that Charbonnet will take team reps in practice this week but will not play against San Francisco, which points to Week 6 at the earliest. Jadarian Price is on IR until Week 8. Wilson handled 75% of the backfield carries in Sunday's win over the Chargers, with 81 rushing yards, three catches for 39 yards and two total TDs.
events.so_what: Wilson is a FLEX start again in Week 5 on volume and goal-line work. Charbonnet is a stash that turns into a committee around Week 6.

events.headline: Ben Johnson names Tyson Bagent the Bears starter for Week 5 vs. Packers with Caleb Williams (hamstring) out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. After Bagent went 25 of 34 for 268 yards and an interception in the 23-12 win over the Jets, Johnson said Monday: "Tyson will be the guy, and we'll go forward from there." Williams remains out with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
events.so_what: Keep Williams benched. Bagent moved the ball well enough that the Bears skill players are startable on their roles, but he is not a fantasy QB start. This is the Monangai and Swift backfield's game to carry.

events.headline: Ollie Gordon runs for 100 yards and a TD as the Dolphins' lead back vs. Vikings
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. With Jaylen Wright back from his stinger and Jeff Hafley having described a split, Gordon still led the Miami backfield in Week 4: 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 22 snaps, about 56% of the backfield share.
events.so_what: Gordon has the early-down and goal-line role behind the departed De'Von Achane and is a FLEX start on that. A 56% share is still a committee, so Wright keeps some standalone value and Gordon is not a locked RB2 yet.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith inactive vs. Rams and unlikely for Week 5; Goedert, Brown, Lane Johnson also out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Smith (hamstring), Hollywood Brown, Dallas Goedert, LB Zack Baun and OTs Lane Johnson and Fred Johnson are on the Eagles' official inactive list. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Smith is unlikely to return in Week 5 against Jacksonville. Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon take the receiver snaps, and Zach Ertz the extra tight-end work.
events.so_what: Bench all three, and plan on Smith missing Week 5 too. Wicks is the WR who absorbs volume and a deep FLEX this week; with two starting tackles out, temper expectations for the whole Eagles passing game. Wicks is the Tuesday FAAB target over Lemon.
